## How the guide defines it

p. 2 glosses the endpoints: `OL – Opening Line`, `CL – Closing Line`, `OT – Opening Total`, `FT – Final Total`, `MOV – Margin of Victory`.

## How the guide uses it

On 16 pages. The vocabulary is glossed and the endpoints appear in historical team tables, but the guide contains no feature on how lines move or how to trade them. Where contributors engage with the market they do so on price levels rather than movement — Buonantony comparing two teams priced level in one market and 2-1 apart in another, Moss telling readers to shop because the numbers vary by book.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

The change in a betting line between when it opens and when it closes, driven by money and information.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the market's own record of what it learned, and the standard external benchmark for whether a bet was good independent of whether it won.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Barely, as a live concept. The guide is a preseason publication whose futures prices are snapshots; it gives a reader the vocabulary and the opening and closing figures for past seasons without building a method on them.
